claim: T5 removes `Gc::sampleRefListQuality` and its `ref_list_probe` call, so a regular GC round no longer performs a second full ref-prefix LIST for store-quality sampling.

`PoolConfig::gc_probe_a_period` was a `PoolConfig` field only: it had no `DECLARE` entry in `ContentAddressedSettings.cpp`, no XML or DDL binding, and was read from `store->poolConfig().gc_probe_a_period` only by test fixtures.
After probe-A deletion, `Gc::RefScanSummary` retains `changed_shards`, `keys`, `listed_lives`, `logs_by_life`, and `max_log_by_life` because each field has consumers outside `sampleRefListQuality`.

The two holey-LIST tests `OmittedRemoveRecordIsSkippedForever` and `OmittedActivationNeverPermitsDeletingALiveBlob` are retained because they cover skipped-transaction retention-leak and data-loss behavior independently of probe A.
`Gc::enumerateRefPrefix` is retained after probe-A deletion and has exactly two callers: `Gc::listRefPrefix` and the `rebuildBaseline` rebuild path.

The 18 GC phases execute in this order: `lease`, `pre_fold_ref_drain`, `heartbeat_floor`, `defer_decision`, `parent_seal_read`, `fold_ref_group`, `fold_seal_read`, `fold_ref_intake`, `fold_reduce`, `fold_seal_write`, `pending_deletes`, `meta_pool_wait`, `round_commit`, `handoff_reclaim`, `manifest_deletes`, `namespace_cleanup`, `ref_object_cleanup`, `orphan_sweep`.

The converted test `CasRetirementSweep.TheRoundEnumeratesTheRefPrefixExactlyOnce` requires one `casRefsPrefix()` LIST per folding round and a positive count for the separate `namespaceRootPrefix()` janitor page.
The historical alternative of widening probe A was rejected; probe A is deleted outright rather than demoted or retained as a sampling mechanism.
The stateless test tag is `no-cas-storage`; the former `no-content-addressed-storage` tag is no longer used.

CAS test-job options resolve through `--cas-storage` and `--cas-s3-storage`; the former `--content-addressed-storage` and `--content-addressed-s3-storage` options are not accepted by `tests/clickhouse-test` or `tests/config/install.sh`.
The stateless CAS job identifiers use the forms `stateless_tests_*_cas_storage_*` and `stateless_tests_*_cas_s3_storage_*`.

The CAS settings are named `deduplication_cache_bytes`, `deduplication_head_first_min_bytes`, and `gc_snapshot_generations_to_keep`; no compatibility alias for the former abbreviated names is provided.

`deduplication_head_first_min_bytes` sends a `HEAD` request before the upload body when `source.size >= cfg.deduplication_head_first_min_bytes`, allowing an already-present upload to be skipped; `0` disables this behavior.

`CasRetirementSweep.TheRoundEnumeratesTheRefPrefixExactlyOnce` classifies LIST calls by exact equality against `layout().casRefsPrefix()` (`cas/ns/stream/`) and `layout().namespaceRootPrefix()` (`cas/ns/`), so the janitor page cannot be counted as a hot ref-prefix scan.

The exactly-once enumeration anchor counts LIST calls for the whole ref prefix, not a total LIST budget: legitimate pagination would count greater than one, while replacing the full-prefix LIST with narrower per-namespace LISTs would not be detected.
`build/cas_suites.txt` contains bare suite names, so a full gtest gate filter must append `.*` to each suite name; a colon-joined filter of bare names can run zero tests and still exit with status 0.

`utils/ca-soak/soak/signals.py` lists `("fold_ref_list", "ref_folding_aborted")` in `DETECTOR_METRICS`, but the server emits the metric under phase `fold_ref_group`; `summarize_phases` silently skips the missing phase, so `fold_ref_list.ref_folding_aborted` never appears in the detector summary or formatted operator line.
`_DETECTOR_COLUMNS` still stores `ref_folding_aborted` as a scalar on the `fold_ref_group` phase row even though the detector-summary key is dead.

The durable fix for the dead `DETECTOR_METRICS` phase key is to rename its phase to `fold_ref_group`, update the three synthetic fixtures, and fail closed when a configured detector phase is absent while other `fold_*` phases exist.
The kept holey-LIST tests use `ASSERT_TRUE(b->holeServed())` as an anti-vacuity guard, so they fail if the list sabotage never fires before asserting `blobPresent()` behavior.
`UniversePolicy::kDefault` is `Authoritative`; the destructive gate requires an authoritative universe, `frontier_namespaces > 0`, and `frontier_proven == frontier_namespaces`.
When the frontier is not complete, destructive work is suppressed pool-wide because blob in-degree is pool-wide and there is no ownership partition of the blob space.

The first statement of the ref walk's `while (expected)` loop is `if (*grounding->committed_through < *expected)`, and `grounding` is not reassigned while `expected` re-enters through that ceiling, so every later body statement runs with `*expected <= *grounding->committed_through`.

Because the committed-through ceiling is always satisfied inside the walk body, a missing record below the ceiling always takes the hold path and cannot take the removed `frontier_proven = true` path.

Ref-walk termination relies on `_ckpt.committed_through` being a round-start snapshot read once per namespace; the remaining proof-producing exits are `resolved_through == *grounding->committed_through` and `nextRefLogIdWithinCommittedFrontier` returning `nullopt` after an applied record.

`FrontierDeficit` preserves the invariant `sum(buckets) == frontier_namespaces - frontier_proven`; every unproven namespace is counted once, and `unattributed` remains the default fence for an exit that names no cause.

The `fold_reduce` phase publishes `frontier_complete` alongside `suppress_destructive`, allowing tests and operators to read the gate's verdict instead of recomputing `namespaces > 0 && proven == namespaces` from a tally.
`StageA_Suppressed` remains the name of a live negative-policy enumerator even after Stage A; a follow-up rename such as `NoUniverseSupplied` would touch about 12 sites.

The historical T6a deficit was caused by records appended above the old frozen tail; commit `357cf7b963f` introduced `_ckpt.committed_through` as the walk ceiling and proves the frontier at that ceiling instead of abandoning it.

A record arriving after a round's LIST is either at or below `committed_through`, where the walk folds it, or above it, where the walk stops at the ceiling with `resolved_through == *committed_through`; neither case leaves the namespace unproven.

Except for `append_above_frozen_tail` and `unattributed`, every frontier-deficit bucket carries an anomaly, hold, or its own warning; therefore a deficit with zero anomalies and zero holds can only be explained by the frozen-tail edge or an unattributed exit.

A healthy-pool soak must require `frontier_proven == frontier_namespaces` on every round, `unattributed == 0`, `probe_budget == 0` or a sufficiently raised `gc_frontier_probe_budget`, and a pending-reclaim backlog that drains to zero and stays there.
When a frontier deficit is nonzero, the suppression warning appends `unproven: <bucket>=<count>, ...`; rounds with no deficit omit the clause.

`suppress_destructive` is computed as `!report.anomalies.empty() || !carried_holds.empty() || frontier_incomplete`; the authoritative flip changes only the value of `universe_authoritative` in the `frontier_complete` expression.

`planManifestCursorPage` may recover debris only for a catalog-named namespace when `catalog_recovery_authoritative` is true; it still requires `prefixEligible`, rejects `Creating` state, survives the protection-view try/catch, and checks active keys before nomination.

The frontier-deficit buckets sum structurally to `frontier_namespaces - frontier_proven`: each unproven target names one bucket, while `probe_budget` and `fold_aborted` are added outside the per-namespace loop.

`CasListLiarEndToEnd.AnEntirelyHiddenNamespacesEdgeIsRefusedByTheProductionDefault` does not test its claimed member-count frontier failure because `buildKillShot` writes no `_ckpt` for either namespace; both namespaces take the `checkpoint_unusable` anomaly path and the test would pass even if the universe term were removed.

`CasGcFrontierGate.HiddenPlusOneInAnUnknownNamespaceIsRefusedByTheProductionDefault` now asserts `frontier_complete == true` and `suppress_destructive == false`, so its test name and section header state the opposite of the behavior being verified.
An authoritative empty universe is not a complete frontier: `frontier_namespaces > 0` is required so `0 == 0` cannot open destructive work.

The production path can prove a catalog-named namespace hidden from LIST by probing its exact ref-log keys; if the namespace is grounded and its folded in-degree reaches zero, the blob is reclaimed on a complete frontier rather than protected by a global suppression switch.

A frontier-probe budget suppressor must be pinned by deleting the namespace `_ckpt`, hiding its prefix, and asserting `frontier_unprobed_budget > 0`; leaving `_ckpt` in place allows the namespace to be proven without consuming the budget.

After the destruction flip, the dropped-pool-member integration test expects janitor residue to drain to `janitor_pending == 0`, while checking `lifeless_keys=0` on every poll and retaining final `dangling=0` and `unaccounted=0` checks.

`planManifestCursorPage` is called only when `!suppress_destructive`; at that point `frontier_complete` implies `universe_authoritative`, so its `catalog_recovery_authoritative` argument is true whenever the gate opens.
CAS integration configs use `<metadata_type>cas</metadata_type>` and the relink test asserts the wire literals `cas_pool_uuid`, `cas_relink=part_manifest_v2`, and `cas_source_token`.

The legacy settings `<content_addressed_allow_shared_pool>` and `<content_addressed_gc_grace_sec>` were removed from CAS integration configs because unrecognized keys reach `impl->set` and raise an exception after Task 3 removed them from `non_cas_keys`.
CAS soak system-log sections and tables are named `cas_log` and `cas_gc_log`; `cas_garbage_collection_log` is not the configured section name.

The system tables `system.content_addressed_log`, `system.content_addressed_garbage_collection_log`, and `system.content_addressed_mounts` no longer exist; live soak tooling queries their CAS-renamed counterparts.
`content_addressed_gc_grace_sec` is rejected as an unknown setting and there is no core retire-grace throttle associated with it.
The asynchronous metric `ReaderExecutorModeledCostMsPerRequestedMiB` was removed from `ServerAsynchronousMetrics::updateImpl` and `ServerAsynchronousMetrics.h`.
The ProfileEvents `ReaderExecutorModeledCostMicroseconds` and `ReaderExecutorRequestedBytes` remain defined even though the asynchronous modeled-cost metric was removed.
The renamed test `04328_reader_executor_modeled_cost_profile_event` verifies `ProfileEvents['ReaderExecutorModeledCostMicroseconds'] > 0` in `query_log`; it no longer tests asynchronous metrics.

`planManifestCursorPage` freezes LIST candidates and exact-GET bytes and tokens before `readAdoptedFoldSeal` and the `CasRefCatalog::read` cut; it performs no fresh GET after the cut, rejects identity mismatches with `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and a token change prevents `deleteExact`.
The `FrontierDeficit` invariant accounts for budget-skipped namespaces on both sides of the equality, and a ref-fold abort resets the result to `proven = 0` with `fold_aborted = frontier_namespaces`.

The anomaly and carried-hold terms in `suppress_destructive` are structural defense-in-depth: in current in-fold paths they co-fire with frontier incompleteness and cannot be isolated by the existing test seams.

`CasListLiarEndToEnd.AnEntirelyHiddenNamespacesEdgeIsRefusedByTheProductionDefault` is inert for the same reason identified in TEST-1: `buildKillShot` writes no `_ckpt`, so both namespaces take `checkpoint_unusable` instead of testing the claimed hidden-member frontier mechanism.

The janitor drain assertion cannot prove that residue was created because `janitor_pending` may reach zero before the first poll; observing pending residue before draining is inherently racy, although the terminal zero and corruption checks remain meaningful.
